rationales.quote: Talk to me a little bit more about this computer visualization
rationales.explanation: Jillian requests material detail about how the computer-vision solution works.

rationales.quote: I don't think they'd have to pivot. I think that they would add this as an option to search for rural properties.
rationales.explanation: She believes Zillow could add the rural-search functionality without major strategic disruption, weakening the product’s defensibility.

rationales.quote: Okay. And how long have you been up -
rationales.explanation: Jillian asks about the product’s operating history in the context of only one completed transaction.

rationales.quote: What have you been doing wrong? Because you only had one sale.
rationales.explanation: She views the single sale as inadequate traction and questions why it has not been repeated.

rationales.quote: the insurance application, which is very compelling
rationales.explanation: She sees insurance liability assessment as a compelling application of the technology.

rationales.quote: Are you thinking about licensing these capabilities to them?
rationales.explanation: She probes whether licensing to insurance companies could provide the monetization model.

rationales.quote: I think the B2B is your bigger sale - I think licensing this to industries
rationales.explanation: Jillian views licensing the technology to businesses as a stronger commercial opportunity than selling to individual property seekers.

rationales.quote: I think this could be much, much bigger.
rationales.explanation: She believes the range of industrial applications could make the opportunity substantially larger.

rationales.quote: I actually really love that.
rationales.explanation: Jillian positively reacts to the founder’s confident, resilient attitude.

rationales.quote: that's the type of founder you like
rationales.explanation: In the immediate in-room debrief, Jillian characterizes the founder as having appealing founder qualities.

rationales.quote: I don't think he knows his customer.
rationales.explanation: She identifies insufficient customer understanding as a major commercial and go-to-market weakness.

rationales.quote: He doesn't know his customer. Right.
rationales.explanation: Jillian reiterates that the founder has not identified or understood the target customer.

question is queried/neutral, not a negative belief. Greetings, jokes, biography, simple confirmations and bare In/Out without
a reason are not rationales. Distinguish closely related taxonomy definitions; do not add broad redundant labels.
Retain each distinct rationale-bearing target utterance and exact evidence turn. Multiple labels on a turn are allowed only
when distinct concepts are expressed. For a repeated concept in different substantive turns retain each occurrence.
Quotes must be exact nonempty substrings of that turn's attributed_text, never continuation narration or another speaker.
The full text is included for context, but only attributed_text is eligible quote evidence.
Classify timing: original_pitch includes Q&A AND the entire original in-room decision discussion; later_commentary includes
post-pitch interviews, later diligence and subsequent updates; teaser is an opening preview/repeated future clip. Use unclear
when timing is uncertain. Do not use the redacted input cutoff as the end of original in-room discussion. Same-session
reversals stay original_pitch. Immediate investor-only debrief in the same room after the founder exits also stays
original_pitch; it is NOT later_commentary. Reserve later_commentary for separate interviews, diligence or updates. Do not mix retrospective opinions into original-pitch scoring.
Direction is positive/negative/neutral towards investing in this company. Salience primary means a stated major reason, not
merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.

borrow another investor's reasoning, or turn a founder claim into the target's belief. Do not force every taxonomy label.
Extract material questions, concerns, supporting arguments and explicit investment-decision explanations. A neutral factual
question is queried/neutral, not a negative belief. Greetings, jokes, biography, simple confirmations and bare In/Out without
a reason are not rationales. Distinguish closely related taxonomy definitions; do not add broad redundant labels.
Retain each distinct rationale-bearing target utterance and exact evidence turn. Multiple labels on a turn are allowed only
when distinct concepts are expressed. For a repeated concept in different substantive turns retain each occurrence.
Quotes must be exact nonempty substrings of that turn's attributed_text, never continuation narration or another speaker.
The full text is included for context, but only attributed_text is eligible quote evidence.
Classify timing: original_pitch includes Q&A AND the entire original in-room decision discussion; later_commentary includes
post-pitch interviews, later diligence and subsequent updates; teaser is an opening preview/repeated future clip. Use unclear
when timing is uncertain. Do not use the redacted input cutoff as the end of original in-room discussion. Same-session
reversals stay original_pitch. Immediate investor-only debrief in the same room after the founder exits also stays
original_pitch; it is NOT later_commentary. Reserve later_commentary for separate interviews, diligence or updates. Do not mix retrospective opinions into original-pitch scoring.
Direction is positive/negative/neutral towards investing in this company. Salience primary means a stated major reason, not
merely any question. decision_link supports_in/out ONLY if the target links the rationale to the commitment/refusal.
Confidence concerns the annotation, not investment probability. Return reviewed_target_turns containing EVERY supplied target
turn index exactly once, even when it contains no rationale. An empty rationale list is valid if none was expressed.
Be concise: prefer one short exact quote per distinct concept/turn, and a one-sentence explanation. Never claim human validation.

rationales.quote: Talk to me a little bit more about this computer visualization
rationales.explanation: Jillian requests material detail about how the computer-vision solution works.

rationales.quote: I don't think they'd have to pivot. I think that they would add this as an option to search for rural properties.
rationales.explanation: She believes Zillow could add comparable rural-search functionality without a major strategic change, weakening differentiation.

rationales.quote: Okay. And how long have you been up -
rationales.explanation: She asks how long the product has operated to contextualize its single completed transaction.

rationales.quote: What have you been doing wrong? Because you only had one sale.
rationales.explanation: She identifies the failure to repeat the first sale as a major traction concern.

rationales.quote: the insurance application, which is very compelling
rationales.explanation: She regards assessing property liabilities for insurers as a compelling problem and application.

rationales.quote: Are you thinking about licensing these capabilities to them?
rationales.explanation: She explores licensing the technology to insurance companies as a monetization approach.

rationales.quote: So I would live like an agent and get into their head.
rationales.explanation: She indicates that the founder needs substantially deeper customer discovery and understanding of agents.

rationales.quote: I think the B2B is your bigger sale - I think licensing this to industries
rationales.explanation: She sees B2B licensing as a stronger commercial model than the consumer property-search business.

rationales.quote: there are just so many different applications for this data.
rationales.explanation: She believes the data can serve numerous industries and therefore supports a substantially broader opportunity.

rationales.quote: I don't see this as selling to a customer looking for a property.
rationales.explanation: The consumer-search direction presented by the founder does not match Jillian's preferred vision of an industry-facing licensing company.

rationales.quote: I actually really love that.
rationales.explanation: She positively evaluates the founder's confident response after the investors decline.

rationales.quote: that's the type of founder you like
rationales.explanation: In the immediate in-room debrief, she explicitly characterizes him as an appealing type of founder.

rationales.quote: I don't think he knows his customer.
rationales.explanation: She identifies inadequate customer understanding as a major go-to-market weakness.

rationales.quote: He doesn't know his customer. Right.
rationales.explanation: She substantively reiterates that the founder has not identified or understood his customer.
